AI made it cheaper to get an Android app built. It didn't change who owns it, and since 30 September that's what Google checks.

On certified devices in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand, apps installed or updated through seven participating stores, Google Play included, must have their package name registered to a verified developer. Google says it expands globally in 2027.

For most Play apps the registration is already done: Google says over 99% were registered automatically.

The real risk is ownership. A package is bound to the account that registers it. If an agency or freelancer published your app from their own account, the app is registered to them. And a lost signing key can't be recovered.

What we recommend: publish from an organisation account your company owns and invite your agency, us included, as users. Request the D-U-N-S number now. It can take up to 28 days.

The largest voluntary biodiversity credit transaction in history happened in October.

CDC Biodiversité sold $1m worth of credits from its Tourbières Tuile Pradeaux site, 13% of everything this market has sold since 2022. A milestone for France Crédits Biodiversité and for the market.

We asked CDC for the buyer's identification and data, but have not yet received any. Apparently nothing can be shared until communication is agreed between them, which will take at least another month.

This opacity makes us question the overall market's relation to data sharing. By value, 63% of all corporate purchases ever made are anonymous. Most developers publish a price and a volume, and stop there. After four years and more than $8m of sales, the market still has no common approach to transparency.

Without buyer data, potential buyers cannot see that their peers are moving on credits, investors cannot size the demand, developers cannot target their outreach, and the people designing national schemes work from isolated cases. Each anonymous transaction removes data that everyone in the market could benefit from.

In our experience, this market moves forward through trust, and transparency is one of the best ways to build it. Even when a buyer prefers to stay anonymous, for reasons we understand, there is a lot of value in sharing its sector, size, country and reason for buying. The commercial sensitivity is much lower, and it is exactly what the market is missing.

This is the main story in this month's Monthly Market Overview, alongside twenty governments launching the Friends of Credits for Nature and Biodiversity at COP17, Indonesia saying it wants its market to be mandatory, ten countries moving up our Countries ladder in one month, Cercarbono launching its Nature Integrity Methodology at COP31, and the IAPB's new way to price a credit against direct investment.

Could solar and battery storage transform electricity access across Southeast Asia's remote islands?

The Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam are joining forces to accelerate the deployment of solar PV and battery energy storage systems (BESS) in island communities that still depend heavily on diesel generators.

The partnership was launched during COP31, with a focus on attracting investment and turning renewable energy opportunities into practical projects.

Here are some numbers that explain why this matters:
🇵🇭 421 out of 447 off-grid power plants in the Philippines relied on oil as of December 2025.
🔋 On Cobrador Island, a 30 kW solar-plus-storage system reportedly:
Cut electricity generation costs by approximately 50%
Extended electricity supply from 8 hours to 24 hours per day
🇮🇩 Research by Indonesia's IESR also indicates that solar PV paired with battery storage could generate electricity at roughly one-third the cost of diesel under the conditions studied.

Why does this matter for the industry?

This is more than a rural electrification initiative. It highlights a growing opportunity for:

Off-grid and island-scale BESS
Solar-plus-storage microgrids
Distributed energy developers
Project financing and regional partnerships

As Southeast Asia continues to expand its renewable energy capacity, replacing diesel in remote communities could become another important growth market for solar and storage.
